title: Security Sign-off Before Production Release
requirement: A production release must have an explicit, recorded security sign-off from a designated security owner before it is deployed.
rationale: Without a required sign-off, a release can reach production without anyone having actually confirmed its security posture, even if security review steps exist informally elsewhere.

methods.procedure: Confirm the release process requires a recorded security sign-off from a designated security owner before a production deployment can proceed.
Review a sample of recent production releases and confirm each has a recorded security sign-off predating the deployment.
Attempt to trigger a production deployment without the required sign-off and confirm the pipeline or process blocks it.

passCriteria: Every production deployment has a recorded security sign-off predating it.
A deployment attempted without a sign-off is blocked.

title: Incident Response Ownership and Escalation Authority
requirement: An incident response plan must designate a named individual or role with documented authority to declare a security incident and initiate the response process.
rationale: Without a designated owner, incident declaration and escalation can stall while responsibility is unclear during the exact moment speed matters most.

methods.procedure: Confirm the incident response plan names an individual or role with documented authority to declare an incident, and that escalation contacts are current.

passCriteria: The incident response plan names an owner or role with documented authority to declare an incident, and escalation contacts are current, not stale.

title: Time-Boxed Risk Acceptance Review
requirement: A formally accepted risk must have an expiration date and be re-reviewed before it expires; an accepted risk must not silently persist past its review date without a recorded decision to renew, remediate, or reject it.
rationale: The RiskAcceptance schema already requires an expiry date, but nothing currently enforces that expired acceptances are actually revisited — an indefinitely accepted risk with no review point becomes a permanent, unexamined gap.

methods.procedure: Confirm a process exists to track accepted risks approaching or past their expiration date and route them for review.
Review the current set of accepted risks and confirm none are past their expiration date without a recorded renew, remediate, or reject decision.

passCriteria: No accepted risk is past its expiration date without a recorded review decision (renew, remediate, or reject).

title: Third-Party Vendor Security Assessment
requirement: A third-party vendor or service that will process or store the project's data, or that will be granted access to production systems, must undergo a documented security assessment before integration.
rationale: A vendor integrated without assessment can introduce a security gap entirely outside the project's own control surface, one the project's own testing will never catch.

methods.procedure: Confirm a documented security assessment process exists and is required before a new third-party vendor or service is integrated.
Review the vendor list and confirm each vendor with access to project data or production systems has a completed security assessment on file.

passCriteria: Every vendor with access to project data or production systems has a completed security assessment on file.
